title: Elly De La Cruz rejoins Reds after 3 weeks nursing hamstring strain
content:
CINCINNATI — The Cincinnati Reds activated shortstop Elly De La Cruz on Tuesday ahead of their game against the National League Central-leading Milwaukee Brewers.

De La Cruz, 24, was placed on the IL with a strained right hamstring after leaving the May 31 game against the Atlanta Braves when he came up limping while approaching first base on a single. The last-place Reds went 7-12 in his absence and fell from six games out of first place in the division to 10 1/2. They are now three games out of a wild-card spot.

De La Cruz was 2-for-8 with a walk and three strikeouts in his three-game rehab assignment with Triple-A Louisville this past weekend. He hit a 441-foot home run in his second plate appearance. On Monday, De La Cruz returned to Cincinnati and took live batting practice against injured closer Emilio Pagán.

This story will be updated.
